High F-tag exposure area. | ⚠️ QA FLAG: No specialist HSTM audience category exists for Infection Preventionist. Mapped to 'Clinical, Non-Medication Dispensing' as interim. Jurisdiction Role: Facility senior leadership and quality improvement teams
Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
Training Topic / Competency Item: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program - Program Overview: a voluntary three-level quality recognition program for long-term care organizations,  based on the Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework. Designed to evaluate organizational strengths, identify improvement opportunities, and drive excellence in clinical and operational outcomes beyond minimum regulatory compliance. Bronze requires foundational process deployment; Silver requires systematic approach alignment across the organization; Gold requires advanced integration of approaches and sustained, benchmarked results across all 7 Baldrige categories.
Frequency: Annual application cycle (award levels are cumulative)
Notes / Research Flags: Not a training mandate - a quality recognition framework. Inclusion in this tracker reflects HealthStream product positioning opportunity: facilities actively pursuing AHCA/NCAL award levels require structured workforce development activities across all 7 Baldrige categories, representing above-compliance training investment. Award-seeking facilities are high-propensity buyers for competency-based learning content. AHCA describes this framework as the basis for evaluating 'strengths, opportunities, and improvement in clinical and operational outcomes.'

Jurisdiction Role: Senior leadership (Administrator, Director of Nursing, Department Heads)
Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
Training Topic / Competency Item: Leadership: senior leaders must define, communicate, and deploy organizational values, vision, and mission; create and sustain a culture of resident-centered excellence and ethical behavior; and personally lead organizational learning and improvement. Requires evidence of leader visibility, accountability systems, two-way communication with workforce and residents, and governance oversight. SNF application: administrator and DON modeling evidence-based leadership behaviors, setting and cascading quality goals, ensuring regulatory and ethical accountability, and creating a culture of safety and improvement.
Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 1 of 7. Directly maps to HealthStream leadership development content: servant leadership, change management, culture of safety, and ethical decision-making for long-term care leaders.

Jurisdiction Role: Senior leadership and quality improvement teams
Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
Training Topic / Competency Item: Strategy: the organization develops strategic objectives and action plans aligned with resident needs, workforce capabilities, regulatory environment, and competitive landscape. Requires data-informed goal-setting, deployment of strategic plans across all operational units, and measurement of progress against stated goals. SNF application: quality strategic planning cycles, regulatory compliance roadmaps, workforce development prioritization, Five-Star improvement planning, and alignment of organizational goals with AHCA quality initiatives.
Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 2 of 7. Maps to HealthStream content around healthcare quality strategy, QAPI program design (which overlaps with CMS §483.75), and strategic performance management for long-term care leaders.

Jurisdiction Role: All staff with resident and family contact
Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
Training Topic / Competency Item: Customers (Residents and Families): the organization systematically listens to and engages residents, families, and key stakeholders; identifies needs, preferences, and expectations; and builds relationships that support satisfaction, loyalty, and service recovery. Requires structured feedback mechanisms, complaint resolution processes, and customer segmentation by care need. SNF application: resident-centered care delivery, satisfaction survey administration and action planning, family engagement protocols, grievance resolution systems, and individualized care preference documentation.
Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 3 of 7. Broadest audience applicability - all direct care staff contribute to resident and family experience. Maps to HealthStream person-centered care, communication, and customer service content. Strong overlap with CMS requirements at §483.10 (Resident Rights) and §483.95(b), but Baldrige approach is systematic and outcome-driven rather than compliance-minimum.

Jurisdiction Role: Quality improvement staff, administrative and clinical leadership
Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
Training Topic / Competency Item: Measurement, Analysis, and Knowledge Management: the organization selects, collects, aligns, and uses data and information for performance tracking and improvement decisions. Requires reliable performance measurement systems, comparative benchmarking against industry standards, data integrity processes, and organizational knowledge-sharing mechanisms. SNF application: QM/QI indicator tracking, MDS data analysis and validation, Five-Star Quality Rating driver analysis, CMS Care Compare benchmarking, NHSN infection data reporting, LTC Trend Tracker use, and internal quality dashboard design and deployment.
Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 4 of 7. Maps to HealthStream content around QI fundamentals, data literacy for clinical leaders, MDS accuracy, and QAPI program execution. Highest overlap with CMS QAPI requirements at §483.75 and §483.95(d) - Baldrige Category 4 represents the systematic, above-compliance version of the federal QAPI mandate.

Jurisdiction Role: All staff; HR, education, and workforce development leadership
Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
Training Topic / Competency Item: Workforce: the organization builds a capable, engaged, and high-performing workforce through systems for workforce capability assessment, learning and development, performance management, and employee well-being and satisfaction. Requires structured competency development programs, onboarding quality, engagement measurement, and workforce planning aligned with organizational strategy. SNF application: competency-based training systems, new hire onboarding effectiveness, staff engagement and retention strategies, performance evaluation processes, career ladder development, and learning culture assessment.
Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 5 of 7. The most direct alignment with HealthStream's core product value proposition. Category 5 is essentially a structured framework for the workforce development investment HealthStream enables. Award-seeking facilities need to demonstrate systematic, measured competency development programs.

Jurisdiction Role: Clinical and operational leadership; department heads
Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
Training Topic / Competency Item: Operations: the organization designs, manages, and continuously improves work systems and processes to deliver safe, high-quality, and efficient care and services. Requires process standardization, performance measurement at the process level, emergency preparedness integration, supply chain management, and cross-functional coordination. SNF application: clinical care delivery workflow design, medication management systems, infection prevention program management, fall prevention process standardization, care coordination between disciplines, and emergency/disaster preparedness program integration.
Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 6 of 7. Maps to HealthStream content in clinical operations, infection control, medication management, and emergency preparedness. Significant overlap with CMS §483.80 (IPCP), §483.45 (Pharmacy), and §483.73 (Emergency Preparedness).

Jurisdiction Role: Senior leadership and quality improvement teams
Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
Training Topic / Competency Item: Results: the organization demonstrates sustained performance and measurable improvement across all key result areas - clinical/health outcomes, resident and family satisfaction, workforce outcomes, operational and process performance, leadership and governance, and financial/market performance. Requires trended data across multiple measurement periods, benchmarking against comparable organizations, and demonstration of cause-and-effect linkage between approaches (Categories 1–6) and results. SNF application: Five-Star Quality Rating trajectory, CMS QM scores, NHSN HAI and infection data, staff turnover and retention rates, survey deficiency trend analysis, resident and family satisfaction scores (AHCA/NCAL LTC Trend Tracker), and operating margin performance.
Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 7 of 7. Results category is the capstone - Gold-level applicants must demonstrate results across all seven categories with multi-year trend data and industry benchmarks. Direct alignment with Five-Star Quality Rating system: staffing domain maps to Category 5 results, health inspection domain maps to Category 6 results, QM domain maps to Categories 3–4 results.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
Training Topic / Competency Item: Bloodborne Pathogens (BBP) Training Program: employer must provide training to all employees with occupational exposure at the time of initial assignment and at least annually thereafter. Training must be provided at no cost to the employee during working hours. Must allow opportunity for interactive questions and answers with a knowledgeable person.
Notes / Research Flags: Most-cited OSHA standard in healthcare. Applies to any employee with reasonably anticipated skin, eye, mucous membrane, or parenteral contact with blood or OPIM. Includes nurses, CNAs, housekeeping, laundry, and maintenance staff in SNF/ALF. Training records must be retained 3 years.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: BBP Training Topic - Regulatory text and epidemiology: (A) an accessible copy of the regulatory text of the standard and an explanation of its contents; (B) a general explanation of the epidemiology and symptoms of bloodborne diseases

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: BBP Training Topic - Transmission and Exposure Control Plan: (C) an explanation of the modes of transmission of bloodborne pathogens; (D) an explanation of the employer's Exposure Control Plan and the means by which the employee can obtain a copy of the written plan

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: BBP Training Topic - Engineering controls, work practices, and PPE: (E) an explanation of the appropriate methods for recognizing tasks and other activities that may involve exposure to blood and OPIM; (F) an explanation of the use and limitations of methods that will prevent or reduce exposure including appropriate engineering controls, work practices, and PPE; (G) information on the types, proper use, location, removal, handling, decontamination, and disposal of PPE

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: BBP Training Topic - HBV vaccine, post-exposure evaluation, and hazard communication: (H) information on the hepatitis B vaccine including efficacy, safety, method of administration, the benefits of vaccination, and that the vaccine will be offered free of charge; (I) information on the appropriate actions to take and persons to contact in an emergency involving blood or OPIM; (J) an explanation of the procedure to follow if an exposure incident occurs, including the method of reporting and the medical follow-up that will be made available

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: BBP Training Topic - Signs, labels, and Q&A: (K) information on the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up that the employer is required to provide for the employee following an exposure incident; (L) an explanation of the signs and labels and/or color coding required by this standard; (M) an opportunity for interactive questions and answers with the person conducting the training session

Jurisdiction Role: All Employees Required to Use PPE
Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Training: employer must provide training to each employee required to use PPE. Employee must demonstrate understanding and ability to use PPE properly before being allowed to perform work requiring PPE. Employer must retrain when previous training is rendered obsolete or employee demonstrates inadequate knowledge or skill.
Notes / Research Flags: Training must cover at minimum: when PPE is necessary; what PPE is necessary; how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE; limitations of the PPE; proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal. Employer provides PPE at no cost. Written hazard assessment certification required (§1910.132(d)(2)).

Jurisdiction Role: All Employees Required to Use PPE
Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: PPE Training Topics: (i) when PPE is necessary; (ii) what PPE is necessary; (iii) how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE; (iv) the limitations of the PPE; (v) the proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal of the PPE

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Respiratory Protection Program and Training: employer must establish a written respiratory protection program with worksite-specific procedures and train each employee required to use a respirator. Training must be comprehensible and provided before employee uses a respirator in the workplace. Annual retraining required.
Notes / Research Flags: Applies in SNF/ALF when N95 respirators (or higher) are required for TB, COVID-19 isolation, or other airborne hazard response. Key elements: written program, medical evaluation (by PLHCP), fit testing (annually for tight-fitting respirators), training. PAPRs (loose-fitting) generally exempt from fit test and medical eval under proposed 2025 rule.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Respiratory Protection Training Topics: (i) why the respirator is necessary and how improper fit, usage, or maintenance can compromise its protective effect; (ii) limitations and capabilities of the respirator; (iii) how to use the respirator effectively in emergency situations, including situations in which the respirator malfunctions

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Respiratory Protection Training Topics (continued): (iv) how to inspect, put on and remove, use, and check the seals of the respirator; (v) what the procedures are for maintenance and storage of the respirator; (vi) how to recognize medical signs and symptoms that may limit or prevent the effective use of respirators

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Respiratory Protection - Medical Evaluation and Fit Testing: employer must provide medical evaluation (using OSHA mandatory questionnaire or equivalent, by PLHCP) before employee is fit tested or uses a respirator. Annual fit testing required for all tight-fitting respirators using OSHA-accepted QLFT or QNFT protocol.
Frequency: Medical eval: before initial use; Fit test: annual
Notes / Research Flags: Not a training topic per se but a required program component. Medical eval records retained per §1910.1020. Fit test records retained until next fit test. Note: 2025 proposed rule (90 FR 27878) would remove medical eval requirement for FFRs and loose-fitting PAPRs - monitor for final rule.

Jurisdiction Role: All Employees with Chemical Hazard Exposure
Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Hazard Communication (HazCom) Training: employer must provide employees with effective information and training on hazardous chemicals in their work area at the time of their initial assignment and whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced into their work area. Must cover GHS-aligned Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and labeling.
Notes / Research Flags: In SNF/ALF applies broadly: housekeeping (cleaning agents, disinfectants), laundry (bleach, detergents), dietary (sanitizers), maintenance (lubricants, HVAC chemicals), and nursing (certain medications may trigger). Written HazCom program required. SDS must be accessible to all employees in their work area on all shifts.

Jurisdiction Role: All Employees with Chemical Hazard Exposure
Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: HazCom Training Topics: (1) requirements of the HazCom standard, including rights and responsibilities; (2) operations in their work area where hazardous chemicals are present; (3) location and availability of the written HazCom program including lists of hazardous chemicals and SDS; methods and observations to detect release; physical, health, simple asphyxiation, combustible dust, and pyrophoric gas hazards; protective measures including appropriate work practices, emergency procedures, and PPE; labeling and SDS interpretation

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Training - Control of Hazardous Energy: employer must provide training to ensure employees understand the purpose, function, and restrictions of the energy control program and have the knowledge and skills required for safe application, usage, and removal of energy controls. Retraining required annually (through periodic inspections) or when deficiencies are identified.
Frequency: Initial; annual periodic inspection review; retraining when gaps found
Notes / Research Flags: Applies in SNF/ALF to maintenance and facilities staff who service HVAC, electrical, plumbing, dietary equipment, elevators, and laundry equipment. Three employee categories require role-specific training: (1) authorized employees who perform LOTO; (2) affected employees who operate equipment being serviced; (3) other employees who work in areas where LOTO is used.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: LOTO Training - Authorized Employees: must recognize hazardous energy sources, the type and magnitude of energy in the workplace, and the methods and means necessary to isolate and control energy. Must demonstrate knowledge of the energy control procedures applicable to their work.
Frequency: Initial; retraining when procedures or equipment change

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: LOTO Training - Affected and Other Employees: affected employees must be instructed in the purpose and use of the energy control procedure. Other employees who work in an area where energy control procedures are used must be instructed about the procedure and the prohibition relating to attempts to restart or reenergize machines or equipment that are locked out or tagged out.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Emergency Action Plan (EAP) Training: employer must train a sufficient number of employees to assist in safe and orderly emergency evacuation. Employer must review the EAP with each employee covered by the plan at the time of initial assignment, whenever the employee's responsibilities or designated actions change, and whenever the plan is changed.
Frequency: Initial; when responsibilities or plan changes
Notes / Research Flags: EAP must be in writing (facilities with more than 10 employees) and cover: emergency escape procedures and routes; procedures for employees who remain to perform critical operations; accounting for employees after evacuation; rescue and medical duties; reporting emergencies; designated emergency coordinator. Dovetails with CMS emergency preparedness requirements at §483.73.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Portable Fire Extinguisher Training: where the employer has provided portable fire extinguishers for employee use in the workplace, the employer must provide an educational program to familiarize employees with the general principles of fire extinguisher use and the hazards involved with incipient stage firefighting. Annual review required. If employer opts for an evacuation-only policy, training focuses on recognizing when to evacuate without fighting fire.
Notes / Research Flags: SNF/ALF must choose policy: (a) allow staff to use extinguishers (requires training), or (b) evacuate-only policy (requires only evacuation-focused training per §1910.38). Most facilities adopt a 'pass and evacuate' policy. Training must include: type of extinguisher, PASS technique (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep), when NOT to fight fire, evacuation procedures.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Formaldehyde / Glutaraldehyde Exposure Training: where employees are exposed to formaldehyde or glutaraldehyde at or above the Action Level (0.5 ppm) or STEL (2 ppm), employer must provide training at the time of initial assignment and at least annually thereafter. Training must include health hazards, signs of exposure, methods of protection, and emergency procedures.
Notes / Research Flags: Relevant primarily in SNF settings that use glutaraldehyde (Cidex) for instrument/equipment sterilization. Action Level = 0.5 ppm; PEL = 0.75 ppm TWA; STEL = 2 ppm. Training must cover: formaldehyde hazards (carcinogen, sensitizer); exposure routes; work practices; PPE; emergency procedures; SDS access. Note: many SNFs have transitioned to alternative disinfectants to avoid this standard.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: Occupational Noise Exposure Training: where employees are included in a Hearing Conservation Program (noise levels at or above 85 dBA TWA), employer must provide training annually. Training must include the effects of noise on hearing, purpose and advantages of hearing protectors, and purpose of audiometric testing and test explanations.
Notes / Research Flags: Applies in SNF/ALF kitchen and laundry areas where commercial equipment may exceed 85 dBA. Hearing Conservation Program required at ≥85 dBA TWA. Annual audiometric testing required. Hearing protectors must be available and properly fitted. Training topics: effects of noise on hearing, types and characteristics of hearing protectors, audiometric testing purposes.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
Training Topic / Competency Item: First Aid Training: in the absence of an infirmary, clinic, hospital, or physician that is reasonably accessible in terms of time and distance to the worksite, the employer must ensure that a person or persons are adequately trained to render first aid. First aid supplies must be readily available.
Approval Basis: employer may use approved training programs (e.g., ARC, AHA)
Notes / Research Flags: In SNF/ALF settings, this is partially offset by the presence of licensed nursing staff on-site. However, OSHA still requires designated first aid responders for staff-to-staff emergencies and situations occurring outside of patient care areas. Standard does not specify training content in detail - ARC or AHA first aid certification is the industry standard to meet this requirement.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) - Training and Instruction: every California employer must establish and implement a training and instruction program to provide all employees, including supervisors, with effective training. Training must include instructions on: general safe and healthy work practices relevant to the job; specific hazards and control measures for each employee's work area and tasks; and any new hazards introduced when work practices or materials change. Employee shall receive training upon initial employment and whenever a new hazard is introduced.
Approval Basis: employer-administered; written IIPP required for all CA employers
Frequency: Initial; when new hazards, equipment, or procedures introduced
Notes / Research Flags: IIPP is the foundational Cal/OSHA compliance requirement with NO federal equivalent (federal OSHA has no mandatory written safety program for general industry). Cal/OSHA UNIQUE. All California employers - regardless of size or industry - must have a written IIPP. Key elements: responsible person designation; compliance system; hazard identification; accident/exposure investigation; hazard correction; training and instruction. Updated July 2020: employer must provide written copy of IIPP to employee within 5 business days upon request at no cost.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: IIPP Training Elements - Training must be provided: (A) when the IIPP is established; (B) to all new employees; (C) to all employees given new job assignments for which training has not previously been provided; (D) whenever new substances, processes, procedures, or equipment are introduced to the workplace and represent a new hazard; (E) whenever the employer is made aware of a new or previously unrecognized hazard; (F) for supervisors to familiarize themselves with the safety and health hazards to which employees under their immediate direction and control may be exposed.
Frequency: Initial; when hazards change; annually recommended

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Bloodborne Pathogens (BBP) Training Program: employer must provide training to all employees with occupational exposure at the time of initial assignment and at least annually thereafter. Training must be provided at no cost to the employee and during working hours. Must include interactive Q&A with a knowledgeable person. Cal/OSHA enhancements over federal: explicitly includes Hepatitis C (HCV) protections; post-vaccination testing for HBV antibody strongly encouraged by Cal/OSHA.
Notes / Research Flags: 8 CCR §5193 mirrors 29 CFR 1910.1030 with California-specific enhancements. Key Cal/OSHA difference: explicitly addresses HCV (Hepatitis C) as a bloodborne pathogen; federal standard references HBV and HIV only. Cal/OSHA also strongly expects post-HBV vaccination antibody testing for all occupationally exposed employees. In SNF/ALF: applies to clinical staff, housekeeping, laundry workers (handling soiled linens/PPE). Training records must be retained 3 years.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: BBP Training Topics - Regulatory text and exposure: (A) accessible copy of the regulatory text and explanation of its contents; (B) general explanation of the epidemiology and symptoms of bloodborne diseases including HIV, HBV, and HCV; (C) explanation of the modes of transmission; (D) explanation of the employer's Exposure Control Plan and how employees can obtain a copy.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: BBP Training Topics - Methods and PPE: (E) explanation of appropriate methods for recognizing tasks involving exposure to blood and OPIM; (F) explanation of use and limitations of methods to prevent or reduce exposure including engineering controls, work practices, and PPE; (G) information on types, proper use, location, removal, handling, decontamination, and disposal of PPE; (H) information on hepatitis B vaccine including efficacy, safety, method of administration, benefits, and that it is offered free of charge.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: BBP Training Topics - Exposure incidents and Q&A: (I) information on appropriate actions to take and persons to contact in an emergency involving blood or OPIM; (J) explanation of procedure to follow if an exposure incident occurs, including reporting method and medical follow-up; (K) information on post-exposure evaluation and follow-up the employer must provide; (L) explanation of signs, labels, and color coding required by the standard; (M) opportunity for interactive questions and answers with a knowledgeable trainer.

Jurisdiction Role: All employees with occupational exposure to aerosol transmissible diseases
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Aerosol Transmissible Diseases (ATD) - Training Program: employer must provide training to all employees with occupational exposure to aerosol transmissible diseases at time of initial assignment and annually thereafter. ATDs include tuberculosis (TB), influenza, COVID-19, SARS, measles, varicella (chickenpox), pertussis, and other diseases listed in Appendix A. Training must be provided at no cost during working hours and must allow interactive Q&A with a knowledgeable person.
Approval Basis: employer-administered; written ATD Exposure Control Plan required
Notes / Research Flags: Cal/OSHA UNIQUE - NO federal equivalent. 8 CCR §5199 explicitly covers 'skilled nursing facilities and long-term health care facilities.' Far more comprehensive than federal BBP or respiratory protection standards. Requires: written ATD Exposure Control Plan; airborne infection isolation (AII) room designation; source control; respirator program (N95 minimum for airborne ATDs; PAPR for high-hazard procedures); medical services; vaccination program (seasonal flu offered free); and full training program. SNFs are required to comply with full §5199 requirements as referring facilities when they cannot provide AII care. Cal/OSHA used §5199 as primary enforcement standard during COVID-19.

Jurisdiction Role: All employees with occupational exposure to aerosol transmissible diseases
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: ATD Training Topics - Overview and modes of transmission: (A) modes of transmission of aerosol transmissible pathogens (airborne vs. droplet); (B) the symptoms and nature of aerosol transmissible diseases relevant to the workplace; (C) the employer's ATD Exposure Control Plan and procedures; (D) the employer's source control procedures and patient screening procedures.

Jurisdiction Role: All employees with occupational exposure to aerosol transmissible diseases
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: ATD Training Topics - PPE and respiratory protection: (E) proper selection and use of personal protective equipment; (F) respirator training in accordance with §5144 (Respiratory Protective Equipment) when respiratory protection is used; (G) the employer's medical services procedures, methods for reporting exposure incidents, and post-exposure evaluation procedures; (H) information on vaccines the employer will make available - for each vaccine: efficacy, safety, method of administration, benefits, and that the vaccine will be offered free of charge (including seasonal influenza vaccine).

Jurisdiction Role: All employees with occupational exposure to aerosol transmissible diseases
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: ATD Training Topics - Plan access and Q&A: (I) how employees can access the employer's written ATD Exposure Control Plan and how employees can participate in reviewing the effectiveness of the employer's procedures; (J) an opportunity for interactive questions and answers with a person who is knowledgeable in the subject matter as it relates to the workplace.

Jurisdiction Role: Each employee required to use a respirator
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Respiratory Protective Equipment - Training: employer must train each employee required to use a respirator before they use one in the workplace. Training must be comprehensive, understandable, and recur annually and when workplace conditions change or deficiencies are found. Must cover: why the respirator is necessary; limitations and capabilities; effective use in routine and emergency situations; inspection, donning, removing, and seal checking; maintenance and storage; medical signs and symptoms limiting effective use.
Approval Basis: employer-administered; written respiratory protection program required
Notes / Research Flags: 8 CCR §5144 is substantially equivalent to 29 CFR 1910.134. Applies in SNF/ALF wherever respiratory protection is required - primarily: N95 respirators for TB isolation (§5199 ATD), COVID-19 aerosol precautions, and certain disinfectants (glutaraldehyde per §5193). Tight-fitting respirators require annual fit testing (QLFT or QNFT). Medical evaluation by PLHCP required before initial use. Note: 2025 federal proposed rule would remove medical eval for FFRs/loose-fitting PAPRs; Cal/OSHA has not yet adopted this change.

Jurisdiction Role: Each employee required to use a respirator; respirator users
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Respiratory Protection - Medical Evaluation and Fit Testing: medical evaluation (using OSHA mandatory questionnaire or equivalent, evaluated by PLHCP) must be completed before initial respirator use and before fit testing. Annual fit testing required for all tight-fitting respirators using Cal/OSHA-accepted QLFT or QNFT protocol.
Frequency: Medical eval: before initial use; Fit test: annual
Notes / Research Flags: Fit test records retained until next fit test. Medical evaluation records retained per §3204. Cal/OSHA has not adopted proposed 2025 federal rule removing medical evaluation requirements for FFRs; California's requirements remain stricter than federal on this point.

Jurisdiction Role: Each employee required to use personal protective equipment
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) - Training: employer must provide training to each employee required to use PPE. Training must cover: when PPE is necessary; what PPE is necessary; how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE; limitations of the PPE; and proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal. Employee must demonstrate understanding and ability to use PPE properly before being allowed to perform work requiring PPE.
Notes / Research Flags: 8 CCR §3380 mirrors 29 CFR 1910.132. Employer must conduct written workplace hazard assessment to identify PPE needs. PPE provided at no cost to employees. Applies across all employee categories - clinical, housekeeping, dietary, maintenance. Retraining required when workplace hazards change, PPE types change, or employee demonstrates inadequate knowledge or skill.

Jurisdiction Role: Employees who may be exposed to hazardous chemicals in their work area
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Hazard Communication (HazCom) - Training: employer must provide employees with effective information and training on hazardous chemicals in their work area at the time of initial assignment and whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced. Training must cover: the requirements of the HazCom standard; operations in their work area where hazardous chemicals are present; location and availability of the written HazCom program, lists of hazardous chemicals, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS); methods and observations to detect chemical releases; physical, health, and other hazards of chemicals; protective measures including PPE; and how to read labels and SDS.
Frequency: Initial; when new chemical hazards introduced
Notes / Research Flags: 8 CCR §5194 mirrors 29 CFR 1910.1200 (GHS-aligned). In SNF/ALF: applies to housekeeping (cleaning agents, disinfectants), laundry (bleach, detergents), dietary (sanitizers), and maintenance staff. SDS must be accessible at all times on all shifts. Cal/OSHA adopted GHS labeling and SDS (16-section format) aligned with federal HazCom 2012. Employer must maintain a list of all hazardous chemicals in the workplace.

Jurisdiction Role: All employees covered by the energy control program
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) - Training and Communication: employer must provide training to ensure that employees understand the purpose, function, and restrictions of the energy control program. Must train employees in accordance with their roles: authorized employees who perform LOTO; affected employees who operate equipment being serviced; other employees who work in areas where LOTO is used. Retraining required when energy control procedures are revised or when periodic inspection reveals deviations.
Frequency: Initial; retraining when procedures or equipment change
Notes / Research Flags: 8 CCR §3314 mirrors 29 CFR 1910.147. Applies to maintenance and facilities staff servicing HVAC, electrical, plumbing, dietary equipment, elevators, and laundry equipment in SNF/ALF. Three-tier training: (1) authorized employees who apply LOTO; (2) affected employees who operate equipment being serviced; (3) other employees who work in LOTO areas. Annual periodic inspection of energy control procedures required.

Jurisdiction Role: Authorized employees; affected employees; other employees in areas where energy control procedures are used
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: LOTO Training Topics: (i) Authorized employees - must recognize applicable hazardous energy sources, the type and magnitude of energy in the workplace, and the methods and means necessary to isolate and control hazardous energy; (ii) Affected employees - must be instructed in the purpose and use of the energy control procedure; other employees who work in areas where energy control procedures are used must be instructed about the procedure and the prohibition against restarting or reenergizing machines or equipment that are locked out or tagged out.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Workplace Violence Prevention in Health Care - Training: employer must provide effective training to all employees that addresses the workplace violence risks they are reasonably anticipated to encounter in their jobs. Training must be provided at time of hire and annually. Employees and their representatives must be allowed to participate in developing training curricula. Training must be specific to the unit, service, or operation where the employee works.
Approval Basis: employer-administered; written WVP Plan required (part of IIPP)
Notes / Research Flags: Cal/OSHA UNIQUE. 8 CCR §3342 applies to all 'health care facilities' to which persons are admitted for a 24-hour stay or longer (HSC §1250 facilities). SNFs are explicitly covered. ALFs/RCFEs (HSC §1569) are NOT covered by §3342 - they fall under SB 553 / Labor Code §6401.9 (general industry WVPP, effective July 1, 2024). §3342 requirements: written unit-specific WVP Plan as part of IIPP; hazard assessment; staffing/engineering controls; violent incident log; post-incident review; annual evaluation. Four types of workplace violence defined: Type 1 (criminal), Type 2 (patient/visitor), Type 3 (employee-on-employee), Type 4 (personal relationship).

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: WVP Training Topics - All Employees: (A) the workplace violence prevention plan applicable to the employee's work area, including the violent incident reporting system and how to report incidents without fear of reprisal; (B) the risk factors and types of workplace violence that the employee is likely to encounter in their job; (C) prevention and avoidance techniques and procedures for the specific work environment; (D) de-escalation techniques and how to respond to violence; (E) how to obtain assistance from law enforcement or emergency services during an incident.
Approval Basis: employer-administered; employee participation in curriculum development required
Notes / Research Flags: Training must be tailored to each unit's specific hazards - a one-size-fits-all annual module does not satisfy §3342. Different content required for: clinical care units (patient aggression, Type 2 violence); administrative areas; emergency response. Post-incident debriefing and trauma-informed support required following violent incidents.

Jurisdiction Role: All employees who perform outdoor work when the outdoor temperature equals or exceeds 80 degrees Fahrenheit
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Heat Illness Prevention (Outdoor) - Training: before commencing outdoor work in heat, employer must provide training on: environmental and personal risk factors for heat illness; employer's procedures for complying with §3395 requirements; importance and methods of acclimatization; different types, signs, and symptoms of heat illness; procedures for first aid and emergency response to heat illness; the importance of drinking water frequently, resting in shade, and acclimatizing; employees' rights including the right to call emergency services. Applies when outdoor temperature at or above 80°F.
Frequency: Before commencing outdoor work; annual refresher
Notes / Research Flags: Cal/OSHA UNIQUE. §3395 is one of the most comprehensive outdoor heat standards in the US - no federal equivalent for general industry. In SNF/ALF: applies to grounds maintenance, outdoor transport/loading, parking lot attendants, and any staff who perform outdoor work. High-heat procedures trigger at 95°F: mandatory 10-minute cool-down rest every 2 hours, close observation of new/returning employees, effective communication systems. Shade must be available within easy reach when temps ≥80°F.

Jurisdiction Role: Employees who work in areas where the indoor temperature may equal or exceed 82 degrees Fahrenheit
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Indoor Heat Illness Prevention - Training: before working in areas where the indoor temperature is 82°F or higher, employer must train employees on: environmental and personal risk factors for heat illness in indoor environments; the employer's procedures for compliance with §3396; the signs and symptoms of heat illness; the importance of drinking water; procedures for first aid and emergency response; employee's right to call emergency services; how to contact the employer in an emergency. Additional training for supervisors on monitoring, recognizing heat illness, and emergency procedures.
Purpose: Before working in covered area + When conditions change
Frequency: Before working in covered area; annual refresher
Notes / Research Flags: Cal/OSHA UNIQUE. 8 CCR §3396 took effect July 23, 2024 - NO federal equivalent. In SNF/ALF: applies to commercial kitchens, laundry rooms, and mechanical rooms where temperatures routinely exceed 82°F. Requirements: cool-down rest (10 min) when employee requests; cool-down area maintained at ≤82°F; cool drinking water; observation of new employees for 14 days; written Indoor Heat Illness Prevention Plan as part of IIPP. Exceptions: work areas where the indoor temp exceeds 82°F for less than 15 min per hour.

Jurisdiction Role: Employees who perform work involving repetitive motion that has caused or is causing work-related repetitive motion injuries
Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Ergonomics / Musculoskeletal Injury Prevention Program (MIPP) - Training: when two or more employees performing the same or similar repetitive motion tasks have developed repetitive motion injuries (RMIs) within a 12-month period, employer must establish a MIPP that includes employee training. Training must cover: specific risk factors and work conditions causing or contributing to the RMIs; methods employees can use to minimize risk, including proper body mechanics and use of available equipment; and procedures for employees to report RMI symptoms early.
Purpose: When MIPP is triggered (2+ RMIs in 12 months)
Frequency: When MIPP is established; when risk factors change
Notes / Research Flags: Cal/OSHA UNIQUE. 8 CCR §5110 is California's general industry ergonomics regulation - NO federal equivalent (federal ergonomics standard was repealed in 2001). In SNF/ALF: patient handling, repositioning, and transfers are primary RMI risk activities; frequently affects CNAs, PCAs, and housekeeping staff. MIPP must include: worksite evaluation; control measures (mechanical lifts, transfer belts, adequate staffing); employee training; and an evaluation procedure. Note: Safe Patient Handling requirements (manual lift prohibition) are addressed separately under HSC §1512.5 for SNF.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Access to Employee Exposure and Medical Records - Employee Training and Notification: employer must inform current employees of the existence, location, and availability of records under this section at the time of initial employment and at least annually. Employer must also inform employees of their rights to access exposure and medical records, and provide access to the records upon employee request. Advance notice of planned employee exposure monitoring required under §340.1.
Notes / Research Flags: 8 CCR §3204 mirrors 29 CFR 1910.1020. Cal/OSHA enhancement: §340.1 requires employer to notify employees and their representatives in advance of planned workplace exposure testing required by Cal/OSHA standards and provide opportunity to observe the testing. Records must be retained for 30 years after employee leaves employment. Includes: medical records generated by employer; exposure monitoring records; biological monitoring records.

Oversight / Professional Agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), California Department of Industrial Relations
Training Topic / Competency Item: Recordkeeping and Reporting - Employee Involvement and Training: employer must inform each employee of how to report a work-related injury or illness. Approval Basis: employer-administered; Cal/OSHA Form 300 required for 10+ employees
Notes / Research Flags: 8 CCR §14300 mirrors 29 CFR 1904 but Cal/OSHA has additional reporting requirements. Key CA difference: employer must report work-related fatalities and serious injuries (hospitalization, amputation, loss of eye) to Cal/OSHA within 8 hours. Cal/OSHA Form 300 required for facilities with 10+ employees. Workplace violence injuries must be recorded. Annual Form 300A summary must be signed by a company executive and posted.
